title: Payroll Calculator
spec: Calculate gross pay using regular hours up to forty, time and a half for up to sixty, and double time beyond that. Deduct federal tax at twenty percent if the gross is over one thousand, else fifteen percent, and state tax at a flat five percent. Additionally, deduct twenty dollars if the union flag is true, and fifty dollars if the family plan flag is true. Ensure final net pay does not fall below zero, returning a list of the numbers. Example: for rate twenty and forty five hours without flags, gross is nine hundred fifty, yielding net seven hundred sixty. The entry function is `payroll(timesheets)`.

title: Bowling Score
spec: Compute the total score for a standard ten frame game from a list of roll numbers using the function `score(rolls)`. Iterate through the frames, treating a first roll of ten as a strike which adds the next two rolls as a bonus. If the two rolls in a frame sum to ten, treat it as a spare and add the next single roll as a bonus, otherwise simply add the two rolls. The tenth frame allows up to three rolls if there is a strike or a spare, which are summed without further bonuses. Return the final integer total. Example: twelve tens yields three hundred.

title: Cart Discounter
spec: Compute the final price for a list of shopping items using the function `checkout(cart)`. Each item has a price, quantity, category, and a clearance flag that prevents any category discounts from applying. For non clearance items, apply a ten percent discount if the category is electronics, or a buy two get one free promotion if it is clothing with a quantity of three or more. Multiply the adjusted price by quantity, and apply an eight percent tax to anything that is not food. If the final sum before tax is under fifty dollars, add a five dollar shipping fee. Return the final total number.

title: Password Validator
spec: Check if a password string meets strict security rules using the function `validate(password)`. The string must be at least twelve characters long, contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, two numbers, and one special character. It cannot contain the word password in any case combination, nor can it contain more than two consecutive identical characters. Finally, the string cannot begin with a number. Return a boolean indicating if it satisfies all rules. Example: a weak string gives false, while a strong valid string gives true.

title: Baggage Fee
spec: Calculate total baggage fees for a list of traveler objects using the function `baggage(passengers)`. The first bag is free if the traveler elite flag is true, otherwise it costs twenty five dollars, while a second bag costs thirty five dollars. Any third bag or beyond incurs a flat one hundred dollar fee each. Additionally, apply a fifty dollar overweight penalty for any bag over fifty pounds, and a seventy five dollar oversize penalty for any bag over sixty two inches. Sum these rules per traveler. Return a list of total fees for each traveler.

title: Poker Evaluator
spec: Evaluate a five card hand where each card object has a suit string and a numerical value using the function `poker(hand)`. Verify if all cards share the same suit to identify a flush, and check if the sorted values are consecutive to identify a straight. If both conditions are met, classify it as a straight flush. Otherwise, count value occurrences to determine if the hand is four of a kind, or a full house if three share one value and two share another. If no special combinations match, fall back to identifying the highest card value present. Return the matching hand rank as a descriptive string.

title: Leap Year Date Parser
spec: Parse a date provided as a string with year, month, and day separated by dashes using `parse(datestring)`. Split the string to verify exactly three numeric parts, ensuring the year is positive and the month falls between one and twelve. Validate the day is correct for the month, accounting for thirty days in september, april, june, and november, and thirty one for the rest. For february, check for a leap year, which occurs when the year is divisible by four but not by one hundred, unless it is also divisible by four hundred. Return a list of the three parsed numbers if valid, or an empty list if any validation check fails.

title: Traffic Light State
spec: Simulate a traffic intersection starting in the red state by processing a list of event strings with `traffic(events)`. If the event is timer, transition from red to green, green to yellow, or yellow back to red. If the event is an emergency, immediately change the state to red regardless of the current state, while a pedestrian event during a green state changes it to yellow. If a flash event occurs, change to a blinking yellow state, which transitions to red upon the next timer event. Process all events sequentially and return the final state as a string.

title: Vending Machine
spec: Simulate a vending machine that dispenses products using the function `vend(actions)`. Maintain a running balance starting at zero, adding coin values to the balance when an insert action occurs. For a select action, check if the balance covers the product price, and if so, record the product name, calculate the change, and reset the balance to zero while ignoring the selection if funds are insufficient. If a refund action occurs, output the current balance as change and reset it to zero. Return a list containing all dispensed product names and any given change amounts.

title: Elevator Routing
spec: Process lift requests containing a target floor number and a direction string using `elevator(requests)`. Starting at floor one heading upwards, separate requests into those above needing to go up, and those needing to go down. First, collect all upward floors in ascending order, ignoring duplicates, but if an emergency flag is present anywhere, immediately clear the queue and route to floor one. After finishing upward requests, reverse direction and process the downward sequence in descending order. Return the final list of floors visited in exact sequential order.

title: Tax Brackets
spec: Calculate progressive income tax for a list of numeric incomes via `taxes(incomes)`. First, subtract a standard deduction of twelve thousand, treating any resulting negative income as zero. The first ten thousand of taxable income is taxed at zero percent, the amount up to forty thousand is taxed at twelve percent, up to eighty thousand at twenty two percent, and anything above at twenty four percent. Furthermore, if the original gross income exceeds one million, add a five percent surcharge on the excess above one million. Return a list of calculated tax amounts rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Heat Index
spec: Calculate the apparent temperature for a list of weather conditions using the function `heat(weather)`. If the temperature is below fifty degrees, use the standard wind chill formula with the provided wind speed, and if between fifty and eighty, return the temperature as is. For temperatures above eighty, apply the rothfusz regression formula combining temperature and humidity. Subtract a specific adjustment if humidity is below thirteen percent and temperature is between eighty and one hundred twelve, or add an adjustment if humidity is above eighty five percent and temperature is between eighty and eighty seven. If the final calculated result is above one hundred, append a severe danger warning to the string output, returning a list of the final results.

title: Roman Numeral
spec: Convert a list of ancient numeral strings to standard numbers with `roman(strings)`. Iterate through each string, looking up the value of each symbol to maintain a running total. If a symbol representing a smaller value appears immediately before a larger one, subtract the smaller value from the total instead of adding it. Ensure that symbols like V, L, and D never repeat, and that other symbols do not repeat more than three times consecutively. If any invalid character or illegal repetition is encountered, output negative one for that string, returning a list of all computed totals.

title: Airline Mileage
spec: Calculate earned frequent flyer miles for a list of flight segments using `mileage(flights)`. The base miles equal the flown distance, but if the distance is under five hundred miles, bump the base up to five hundred. Reduce the base miles by fifty percent for basic economy class, add a fifty percent bonus for business class, and add a one hundred percent bonus for first class. Add a flat five hundred mile bonus if the international flag is true, and finally multiply the entire total by one point five if the elite flag is true. Sum all earned miles across the segments and return the total as an integer.

title: Markdown Converter
spec: Convert a list of text lines into basic web formatting tags using `markdown(lines)`. Return an empty string for empty lines, wrap lines starting with a hash and a space in a header one tag, wrap lines starting with a greater than sign in a blockquote tag, and wrap lines starting with a dash and space in a list item tag. For any other text, wrap the line in a standard paragraph tag. Additionally, scan all text to replace words surrounded by double asterisks with strong tags, and words surrounded by single asterisks with emphasis tags. Return the list of fully formatted strings.

title: IP Validator
spec: Validate and classify a list of internet address strings with the function `network(addresses)`. Split each string by the dot character to verify it has exactly four numeric parts that fall between zero and two hundred fifty five, ensuring no part has leading zeros unless it is a single zero. Classify valid addresses based on the first part: loopback if it is one hundred twenty seven, class a if under one hundred twenty eight, class b if under one hundred ninety two, and class c if under two hundred twenty four. Return a list of the resulting classification strings, or an invalid marker for any address that fails the checks.

title: Inventory Planner
spec: Determine restock amounts for a list of warehouse items using `inventory(products)`. If an item is marked discontinued, mandate an order of zero. Otherwise, calculate the reorder point by multiplying daily sales by lead time and adding safety stock, ordering zero if current stock is at or above this point. If stock is low, calculate a target order to reach twice the reorder point, capping it if it exceeds maximum capacity, and rounding it up to the minimum batch size if it falls short. Return a list of the final order quantities for all items.

title: Recipe Scaler
spec: Scale a list of culinary ingredients from a recipe serving four to serve ten guests using `recipe(ingredients)`. Multiply the amount of each ingredient by the resulting scale factor of two point five, unless the ingredient is a spice, in which case cap the multiplier at two to avoid overpowering the dish. Convert units to maintain readability: change tablespoons exceeding sixteen into cups by dividing by sixteen, teaspoons exceeding three into tablespoons by dividing by three, and grams exceeding one thousand into kilograms. Return a list of the formatted ingredient phrases with their adjusted amounts and units.

title: Log Parser
spec: Parse a list of text lines from a server log using the function `logs(lines)`. Skip malformed lines that lack surrounding brackets, and for valid lines, extract the timestamp from inside the brackets, the severity level immediately following, and the rest as the message. Keep a running count of total warning levels and total error levels encountered. If an error severity line contains the word timeout in any capitalization within its message, increment a specific timeout error counter as well. Return an array containing the total warnings, total errors, and timeout errors.

title: Meeting Scheduler
spec: Find the first available one hour time block during a workday running from nine morning to five evening with `schedule(meetings)`. The input events have start and end times represented as minutes past midnight, which must first be sorted chronologically by start time. Check if the gap between nine morning and the first event is at least sixty minutes, then iteratively check the gaps between the end of each event and the start of the consecutive one. Finally, check the gap between the end of the last event and five evening. Return the starting minute of the first sufficient gap found, or negative one if no such gap exists.

title: Morse Code
spec: Translate a sequence of dots and dashes separated by spaces into text using `morse(signals)`. A single space delineates letters, while three consecutive spaces delineate distinct words. Split the input by three spaces to isolate words, then split each word by single spaces to isolate letters, and look up each symbol sequence in a standard alphabet mapping. Substitute a question mark for any sequence that is completely unrecognized. Reconstruct the message by joining the resolved letters together, and then joining the words with a single space, returning the final translated string.

title: Tennis Match
spec: Score a single game of tennis from a sequence of point winner strings using `tennis(points)`. Track the scores using love, fifteen, thirty, and forty, processing each point sequentially for either player one or player two. If both players reach forty, transition the game state to deuce, meaning the next point won grants advantage to that specific player. If the player with advantage wins the subsequent point, they win the game, but if the trailing player wins, the score reverts to deuce. Return the winner name if the game completes, or the current score state string if the points run out early.

title: Library Fines
spec: Calculate financial penalties for a list of returned library items with the function `fines(returns)`. If the item lost flag is true, charge a flat fifty dollar replacement fee and skip all daily calculations, and if overdue days are zero or negative, the penalty is simply zero. Otherwise, charge twenty cents per day for regular books up to a ten dollar maximum, fifty cents per day for new releases up to a ten dollar maximum, and one dollar per day for dvds with no maximum limit. Finally, if the patron teacher flag is true, waive the entire penalty if it amounts to less than five dollars. Return a list of the computed charges for each item.

title: Shipping Router
spec: Determine the shipping zone and delivery cost for a list of parcels using `route(packages)`. Classify the zone as local for travel under one hundred miles, regional for up to five hundred miles, and national for anything beyond, setting the base cost to five, ten, and fifteen dollars respectively. Add two dollars for every pound over ten pounds, a twenty dollar freight surcharge if the total weight exceeds fifty pounds, and a five dollar handling fee if the fragile flag is true. If the international flag is true, multiply the final calculated cost by two. Return a list of the computed final costs for all parcels.

title: Bank Loan
spec: Calculate the monthly obligation for a list of loan accounts using the entry point `amortize(loans)`. If the loan jumbo flag is true, add a five hundred dollar origination fee to the principal before calculating. Apply a short term discount by subtracting one percent from the annual interest rate if the term is under five years, ensuring the rate never drops below zero. Convert the annual rate to a monthly decimal and the term years to total months, dividing principal by months if the interest is zero, otherwise applying the standard amortization formula. Return a list of the monthly payments rounded to two decimal places.

title: Cricket Over Simulator
spec: The entry function is `evaluate(balls)`. The input is a list of strings representing deliveries, with valid types being single, double, boundary, sixer, wide, noball, and wicket. A single adds one run, a double adds two, a boundary adds four, and a sixer adds six, with all of these counting as one legal delivery. Wides and noballs each add one run but do not count as legal deliveries, whereas a wicket adds zero runs but does count as a legal ball. The over finishes as soon as six legal balls are bowled, completely ignoring any extra items remaining in the list. Return a list of three numbers representing the total runs scored, legal balls bowled, and wickets lost. For example, given single, wide, wicket, double, boundary, the output is eight, four, one.

title: Escape Room Scorer
spec: The entry function is `score(actions)`. The input is a list of strings detailing player actions in an escape room, such as clue, puzzle, hint, or escape. The base score starts at one thousand points. Finding a clue adds fifty points, and solving a puzzle adds one hundred points. Asking for the first hint deducts twenty points, the second deducts fifty points, and any subsequent hint deducts one hundred points. If the escape action is found within the first ten actions of the list, a time bonus of five hundred points is added, whereas escaping after twenty actions awards no bonus. Return the final integer score. For example, finding a clue, asking for a hint, solving a puzzle, and escaping yields eleven hundred thirty points.

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: The entry function is `rank(arrows)`. The input is a list of numbers representing arrow landing zones from one to ten, with zero representing a complete miss. The logic must group the sequential arrows into ends consisting of exactly six arrows each. For each end, the base score is the simple sum of the arrow values. If an end contains at least three perfect tens, award a bonus of five points for that specific end, but if an end has any misses, deduct two points from that end's total. Sum the scores of all complete ends, completely ignoring any leftover arrows at the end of the list that do not form a full set of six. Return the final total score as an integer. For example, an input of ten, ten, ten, nine, nine, zero followed by six nines yields a score of forty six plus fifty four, totaling one hundred.

title: Coffee Roasting Profiler
spec: The entry function is `profile(temperatures)`. The input is a list of numbers representing minute by minute temperature readings in celsius during a coffee roast. The drying phase occurs while temperatures are below one hundred fifty degrees. The maillard reaction phase begins at one hundred fifty degrees and ends when the temperature reaches two hundred degrees, while the development phase is any temperature at or above two hundred degrees. The logic must count the number of minutes spent in each of the three phases. If the temperature ever drops by more than five degrees from one minute to the next, the roast is considered stalled, and the function must immediately return a list containing negative one for all three phase counts. Otherwise, return a list of the three phase durations. For example, given temperatures of one hundred, one hundred forty, one hundred sixty, and two hundred ten, the output is two, one, one.

title: Gemstone Cutting Yield
spec: The entry function is `facet(rough)`. The input is a list of numbers representing a rough gemstone's weight in carats, its clarity score from one to ten, a binary flag where one means the stone has visible inclusions, and the cutter's skill level from one to five. The base faceted yield is exactly forty percent of the rough weight. If the cutter's skill is four or five, the yield increases by an absolute five percent, whereas a skill of one reduces it by five percent. If the stone has visible inclusions, the cutter must work around them, which removes ten percent of the current calculated yield. Finally, if the clarity score is a perfect ten, an extra cautious cutting process is used to preserve maximum value, reducing the final yield by a further two percent. Return the final faceted carat weight truncated to two decimal places. For example, a ten carat rough with clarity ten, visible inclusions, and a skill five cutter evaluates to three point nine six carats.

title: Mini Golf Scorer
spec: The entry function is `tally(strokes)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the number of strokes taken on each hole of a nine hole miniature golf course, where the par for every hole is three. For each hole, determine the score relative to par. A hole in one always subtracts two from the total score, regardless of par, while taking exactly par adds zero. Taking more than par adds the difference to the total, but the maximum recorded strokes for any single hole is strictly capped at six. If a player skips a hole, represented by a zero, they receive a flat penalty of five points for that hole. Sum the relative scores for all nine holes and return the final integer relative to par. For example, scoring one, three, four, zero, and five threes results in a total of four over par.

title: Crop Rotation Planner
spec: The entry function is `plan(history)`. The input is a list of strings representing the sequence of crops planted in a single field over the past four seasons. The known crop types are legume, brassica, nightshade, and root. The logic evaluates the optimal crop for the upcoming fifth season. If the field has seen a nightshade in the immediately preceding season, planting another nightshade or a root is prohibited to break pest cycles, so the system must recommend grass. If the four season history contains no legumes at all, the primary need is nitrogen fixation, so recommend legume. If any two consecutive seasons in the history contain the exact same crop type, the soil is considered heavily stressed, and the recommendation must be fallow. If none of these conditions are met, recommend brassica as a standard rotational filler. For example, an input of root, root, legume, nightshade evaluates to fallow because of the consecutive roots.

title: Grocery Barcode Checksum
spec: The entry function is `scan(barcode)`. The input is a string of exactly twelve digits representing a standard retail product code. The logic must separate the first eleven digits from the final check digit. It then calculates a checksum by taking the sum of the digits in the odd positions, which are the first, third, fifth, and so on, and multiplying that sum by three. It then adds the sum of the digits in the even positions, up to the tenth position. The total sum is then divided by ten, and the remainder is subtracted from ten to find the calculated check digit, though if the remainder is zero, the check digit is simply zero. Return the word match if the calculated digit equals the final digit of the input, otherwise return the word mismatch. For example, an input of zero three six zero zero zero two nine one four five two returns match.

title: Fantasy Football Scorer
spec: The entry function is `calculate(stats)`. The input is a list of numbers representing a player's weekly statistics in the exact order of passing yards, passing touchdowns, interceptions thrown, rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, and fumbles lost. Passing yards award one point for every full twenty five yards, while passing touchdowns award four points each. Interceptions thrown penalize the score by two points. Rushing yards award one point for every full ten yards, while rushing touchdowns award six points each, and fumbles lost penalize the score by two points. If the player surpasses three hundred passing yards or one hundred rushing yards, they receive a bonus of three points for each milestone successfully reached. Return the total integer score. For example, two hundred fifty passing yards, two passing touchdowns, zero interceptions, forty rushing yards, zero rushing touchdowns, and one fumble lost totals ten points.

title: Real Estate Appraisal
spec: The entry function is `appraise(features)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the square footage, number of bedrooms, number of bathrooms, age of the house in years, and a condition rating from one to five. The base value of the house is the square footage multiplied by one hundred and fifty. Each bedroom adds ten thousand to the value, and each bathroom adds fifteen thousand. For every year of age, one thousand is subtracted from the value, but the maximum age deduction cannot exceed fifty thousand under any circumstances. Finally, the subtotal is adjusted by the condition rating: a rating of one reduces the value by twenty percent, a rating of three leaves it unchanged, and a rating of five increases it by twenty percent. Return the final computed value as a number. For example, a two thousand square foot home with three bedrooms, two bathrooms, ten years old, and a condition rating of three evaluates to three hundred fifty thousand.

title: Train Ticket Pricing
spec: The entry function is `price(details)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the travel distance in miles, the passenger age, a binary flag where one means peak hours and zero means off peak, and another binary flag where one means first class. The base fare is calculated at twenty cents per mile. If the passenger is under twelve years old, they receive a fifty percent discount on the base fare, whereas if they are sixty five or older, they receive a thirty percent discount. If travel occurs during peak hours, a flat surcharge of fifteen is added to the fare. Finally, if first class is selected, the total fare calculated so far is multiplied by one point five. Return the final fare rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, a one hundred mile trip for a ten year old during off peak hours in standard class costs ten.

title: Blood Type Compatibility
spec: The entry function is `match(types)`. The input is a list of two strings representing the donor blood type and the recipient blood type, using designations like O positive, A negative, or AB positive. The logic must determine if a transfusion is medically safe based on standard compatibility rules. An O negative donor can give to anyone, while an AB positive recipient can receive from anyone. A negative rh factor donor can give to either positive or negative recipients, but a positive rh factor donor can only safely give to positive recipients. For the letter groups, A can donate to A or AB, B can donate to B or AB, O can donate to any letter, and AB can only donate to AB. Return the word safe if all conditions are satisfied, or the word unsafe if not. For example, an input of O negative and A positive returns safe.

title: Soil Classification
spec: The entry function is `classify(percentages)`. The input is a list of three numbers representing the percentage of sand, silt, and clay in a soil sample, which must always sum to exactly one hundred. The logic must categorize the soil texture based on dominant traits. If the clay content is forty percent or higher, the soil is categorized as heavy clay. If sand is eighty five percent or higher, it is categorized as sand, and if silt is eighty percent or higher, it is categorized as silt. If the mixture falls in the middle, specifically having less than thirty percent clay, less than fifty percent silt, and less than fifty two percent sand, it is categorized as loam. Otherwise, it is simply classified as mixed. Return the string representing the final category. For example, twenty percent clay, forty percent silt, and forty percent sand returns loam.

title: Aquarium Filter Sizing
spec: The entry function is `size(parameters)`. The input is a list of numbers containing the tank length in inches, width in inches, height in inches, and a bioload rating from one to three. The gross volume in gallons is calculated by multiplying length, width, and height, then dividing that result by two hundred and thirty one. The base required flow rate is four times the gross volume per hour. If the bioload rating is two, representing a moderate fish population, multiply the required flow rate by one point five. If the bioload is three, representing a heavy population or messy eaters, multiply the flow rate by two. Finally, add an extra fifty gallons per hour if the tank volume is over fifty gallons to account for dead flow zones. Return the required flow rate rounded to the nearest integer. For example, a tank of twenty by ten by twelve inches with a bioload of one requires ten gallons, resulting in forty gallons per hour.

title: Ski Resort Lift Pass
spec: The entry function is `charge(traveler)`. The input is a list containing the skier age, the number of consecutive days they intend to ski, and a binary flag indicating if the dates fall during a holiday period where one is true. The standard adult daily rate is one hundred and twenty. Skiers aged twelve and under pay sixty per day, while those aged sixty five and over pay ninety per day. Buying a pass for three or more consecutive days triggers a twenty percent discount on the accumulated base price. However, if the holiday flag is true, a blackout fee of thirty per day is added before any multi day discount is calculated. Return the final total price rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, a ten year old skiing for three days during a non holiday period pays one hundred and forty four.

title: Bicycle Gear Ratio
spec: The entry function is `gear(specs)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the number of teeth on the front chainring, the number of teeth on the rear cog, the wheel diameter in millimeters, and the tire width in millimeters. The total wheel diameter is calculated by adding twice the tire width to the wheel diameter. The gear ratio is determined by dividing the front chainring teeth by the rear cog teeth. The gear inches metric is found by multiplying the gear ratio by the total wheel diameter converted to inches, using a fixed conversion factor of twenty five point four millimeters per inch. Finally, the rollout or development in meters is calculated by multiplying the total diameter in meters by pi, then multiplying by the gear ratio. Return a list containing the gear inches and the rollout in meters, both truncated to one decimal place. For example, fifty teeth front, twenty five rear, six hundred twenty two wheel, and twenty five tire yields roughly fifty two point eight inches and four point two meters.

title: Water Bill Calculator
spec: The entry function is `bill(usage)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the monthly water consumption in gallons for a residential property, followed by a binary flag indicating if the property receives a low income discount. A fixed connection fee of twenty is always applied to the account. For the first five thousand gallons, the rate is two cents per gallon, and for usage between five thousand and ten thousand gallons, the rate increases to three cents per gallon. Any usage above ten thousand gallons is billed at five cents per gallon to discourage excessive waste. A flat drought surcharge of fifteen is added if the total usage exceeds eight thousand gallons. Finally, if the low income flag is one, a twenty five percent discount is applied to the final calculated bill. Return the total bill amount truncated to an integer. For example, four thousand gallons with no discount results in exactly one hundred.

title: Beehive Honey Yield
spec: The entry function is `project(hive)`. The input is a list of numbers containing the average daily temperature in celsius, the number of sunny days in the month, a flora density score from one to ten, and a mite infestation percentage. The base expected honey yield is ten kilograms for a perfectly healthy hive. If the average temperature is below fifteen degrees, the bees are less active and the base yield drops by thirty percent. Each sunny day above twenty total days adds half a kilogram to the expected yield. A flora density score of eight or higher provides a multiplier of one point two to the current total, while a score below four reduces the total by twenty percent. Finally, the mite infestation percentage directly subtracts from the yield, meaning a five percent infestation removes five percent of the final honey amount. Return the projected yield in kilograms truncated to two decimal places. For example, twenty degrees, twenty two sunny days, a flora score of nine, and a two percent infestation yields thirteen point one five kilograms.

title: Paint Coverage Calculator
spec: The entry function is `estimate(dimensions)`. The input is a list of numbers representing room length, width, ceiling height, number of standard doors, and number of standard windows, all measured in feet. The logic calculates the total wall surface area by adding the perimeter of the room and multiplying it by the ceiling height. It then subtracts twenty one square feet for every standard door and fifteen square feet for every standard window. A single gallon of paint is known to cover exactly three hundred and fifty square feet of wall space. The homeowner always requires two coats of paint for a proper professional finish. To ensure they do not run out during the job, add an extra ten percent to the required paint volume as a safety margin. Return the number of gallons needed, rounded up to the nearest whole integer. For example, a ten by ten room with an eight foot ceiling, one door, and one window evaluates to two gallons.

title: Photography Exposure Value
spec: The entry function is `expose(settings)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the camera aperture f-stop, the shutter speed in seconds, and the iso sensitivity. The logic calculates the base exposure value by taking the base two logarithm of the aperture squared divided by the shutter speed. The camera iso must then be accounted for, as the base value was calculated assuming an iso of one hundred. For every doubling of the iso above one hundred, the exposure value increases by one full step. If the final computed exposure value is below zero, the scene is categorized as night. If it is between zero and ten, it is indoor lighting, and if it is greater than ten, it is outdoor daylight. Return a list containing the numerical exposure value truncated to one decimal and the lighting category string. For example, an aperture of two point eight, a shutter speed of one sixtieth, and an iso of four hundred returns ten point nine and outdoor daylight.

title: Chess ELO Rater
spec: The entry function is `rate(match)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the player rating, the opponent rating, the match outcome where one is a win, zero point five is a draw, and zero is a loss, and the number of previous games played by the player. The logic determines the expected score by calculating one divided by the sum of one plus ten raised to the power of the opponent rating minus the player rating divided by four hundred. The rating change is calculated by multiplying a development coefficient by the difference between the actual outcome and the expected score. The development coefficient is forty for players with fewer than thirty previous games, twenty for players rated under two thousand four hundred, and ten for highly rated experienced players. Return the player's new rating rounded to the nearest integer. For example, a one thousand five hundred rated player beating a one thousand six hundred rated player on their tenth game yields a new rating of one thousand fifty three.

title: Pizza Dough Hydration
spec: The entry function is `knead(ingredients)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the weight of flour, water, salt, and fresh yeast in grams. The logic must compute the baker's percentages by dividing the weight of each minor ingredient by the weight of the flour and multiplying by one hundred. The hydration level is defined strictly as the percentage of water. If the hydration is below sixty percent, the dough is classified as stiff, between sixty and seventy percent is standard, and above seventy percent is high hydration. The salt percentage must be checked; if it exceeds three percent, the function should return the string too salty. The baseline proofing time is estimated at twenty four hours at room temperature, but is reduced by two hours for every full percent of yeast above one percent. Return a list containing the string classification and the estimated proofing time in hours. For example, one thousand grams of flour, six hundred fifty grams of water, twenty grams of salt, and twenty grams of fresh yeast returns standard and twenty two.

title: Car Depreciation
spec: The entry function is `depreciate(vehicle)`. The input is a list containing the original purchase price, the vehicle age in years, total mileage, a binary flag for accident history, and a brand tier string of either luxury, standard, or budget. The base depreciation is fifteen percent per year, meaning the car normally retains eighty five percent of its value annually. For a luxury brand, the annual retention rate is dropped to eighty percent, while for a budget brand, the retention rate improves to eighty eight percent. If the mileage exceeds fifteen thousand miles per year of age, an additional deduction of two percent of the current value is applied for each excess thousand miles. Finally, if the accident history flag is one, the total current value is slashed by a flat twenty percent. Return the current estimated value rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, a twenty thousand dollar standard car, one year old, with twenty thousand miles and no accidents, evaluates to sixteen thousand six hundred and sixty.

title: Fitness Calorie Tracker
spec: The entry function is `burn(activities)`. The input is a list of numbers where the first is the user's body weight in kilograms, and the subsequent numbers come in pairs representing an activity intensity level from one to ten and the duration in minutes. The base resting metabolic rate burned per hour is roughly equivalent to the body weight. For each activity pair, the calories burned are calculated by multiplying the weight by the intensity level, then by the duration divided by sixty. If the intensity is eight or higher, the activity is considered vigorous, triggering an afterburn effect that adds a flat fifteen percent bonus to the calories burned for that specific activity. Sum the calories burned across all listed activities and return the total active calories burned as an integer. For example, a seventy kilogram user exercising at an intensity of five for sixty minutes burns three hundred and fifty calories.

title: Board Game Combat
spec: The entry function is `resolve(clash)`. The input is a list of numbers representing the attacker dice roll, attacker weapon strength, defender dice roll, defender armor value, and a terrain advantage flag where one is true. The attacker's total strike power is their dice roll plus their weapon strength. The defender's block power is their dice roll plus their armor value, plus an extra three points if the terrain flag is true. If the defender rolls a natural one, their armor is completely ignored and set to zero. A critical hit occurs if the attacker rolls a natural six, which automatically doubles their total strike power. If the final strike power exceeds the block power, return the numerical difference as damage. Otherwise, the attack is fully blocked and the function must return zero. For example, an attacker rolling six with a weapon strength of two against a defender rolling four with armor three and no terrain advantage results in nine damage.

title: Diving Score Calculator
spec: Implement a `score(dives)` function that calculates the total competition score for a diver. The input is a list of dive records, where each record contains the degree of difficulty and a list of seven integer scores from judges. For each dive, sort the seven judges scores, discard the two highest and two lowest scores, and sum the remaining three scores. Multiply this sum by the degree of difficulty to find the dive total. Return the sum of all dive totals rounded to two decimal places. For example, if a dive has a difficulty of three and scores of seven, eight, seven, nine, eight, eight, and seven, the kept scores are seven, eight, and eight, summing to twenty three, yielding a total of sixty nine.

title: Solar Array Sizing
spec: Write a `size(parameters)` function that determines the minimum number of solar panels required to meet a household energy demand. The input provides the monthly energy usage in kilowatt hours, the average daily peak sun hours, the power rating of a single panel in watts, and the overall system efficiency percentage. First, calculate the daily energy requirement by dividing the monthly usage by thirty days. Next, divide this daily requirement by the product of peak sun hours and system efficiency to find the required total array wattage. Finally, divide the total wattage by the individual panel wattage and round up to the nearest whole number to get the panel count. If usage is nine hundred, sun hours is five, panel rating is three hundred, and efficiency is eighty percent, the output should be twenty five panels.

title: Gymnastics Score Aggregator
spec: Write an `evaluate(routines)` function to compute the final standings for a gymnastics team. The input is a list of gymnast performances, each specifying the gymnast name, an apparatus name, an execution score out of ten, a difficulty score, and a deduction penalty. For each performance, the final mark is the sum of execution and difficulty minus the deduction. If the execution score is below a five, apply an additional mandatory safety deduction of one point. Return a list of gymnast names and their final marks, sorted from highest to lowest mark. For a gymnast with execution eight, difficulty six, and deduction half a point, the final mark is thirteen and a half.

title: Winter Weather Index
spec: Implement an `index(conditions)` function that calculates the perceived temperature based on ambient temperature in Celsius and wind speed in kilometers per hour. The input is a list of weather reading tuples containing temperature and wind speed. For each reading, if the temperature is above ten degrees or the wind speed is below four point eight, the perceived temperature equals the ambient temperature. Otherwise, apply the standard wind chill formula which multiplies the temperature by zero point six two one five, adds thirteen point one two, subtracts eleven point three seven times the wind speed raised to the power of zero point sixteen, and adds zero point three nine six five times the temperature times the wind speed raised to the same power. Return a list of the perceived temperatures rounded to one decimal place.

title: Soap Saponification Calculator
spec: Implement a `saponify(ingredients)` function that calculates the amount of lye and water needed to make cold process soap. The input provides a list of oils with their weights in grams and their specific saponification values, as well as a desired water to lye ratio, and a superfat percentage. First, calculate the total required lye by multiplying each oil weight by its saponification value and summing the results. Next, reduce this total lye amount by the superfat percentage to leave some oils unreacted for skin conditioning. Finally, multiply the adjusted lye amount by the water to lye ratio to find the required water weight. Return a tuple containing the final lye weight and the water weight, both rounded to the nearest whole gram.

title: Snooker Break Scorer
spec: Write a `tally(balls)` function to calculate the total points scored in a continuous snooker break. The input is a list of color names representing the sequence of balls potted. Red balls are worth one point, yellow is two, green three, brown four, blue five, pink six, and black seven. Red balls must be followed by a colored ball until all reds are gone. If the sequence violates the alternating red and color rule during the initial phase, stop scoring and return the points accumulated up to the foul. After the last red and its corresponding color are potted, the remaining colors must be potted in strictly ascending order of their value. Any out of order color in the final phase stops the break. Return the valid accumulated points as an integer.

title: Roulette Payout Settler
spec: Implement a `settle(bets)` function that determines the total net profit or loss for a series of roulette bets after a spin. The input includes the winning number from zero to thirty six, and a list of bet records containing the bet type, the chosen numbers or category, and the wager amount. Single number bets pay thirty five to one. Split bets on two numbers pay seventeen to one. Corner bets on four numbers pay eight to one. Red, black, odd, even, high, and low bets pay one to one. If the winning number is included in the bet, add the payout to the total profit. If it is not, subtract the wager amount. Return the overall net result across all bets.

title: Flight Boarding Grouper
spec: Write a `group(passengers)` function that assigns boarding groups to airline passengers. The input is a list of passenger records containing their frequent flyer tier, ticket class, and whether they need special assistance. Special assistance passengers are always assigned to group one. First class passengers get group two. Business class or elite frequent flyers get group three. Premium economy gets group four. Regular economy gets group five, unless they purchased basic economy, which gets group six. If a passenger qualifies for multiple groups based on tier and class, assign them to the lowest numbered group they are eligible for. Return a list of passenger names paired with their assigned group number.

title: Battery Health Estimator
spec: Implement an `estimate(usage)` function that projects the remaining health percentage of a lithium ion battery. The input is a list of charge cycles, where each cycle specifies the depth of discharge percentage and the operating temperature in Celsius. Start with a baseline health of one hundred percent. For each cycle, if the depth of discharge is greater than eighty percent, subtract zero point zero five percent from the health. If it is fifty to eighty, subtract zero point zero two percent, and if below fifty, subtract zero point zero one percent. Furthermore, if the temperature during the cycle exceeds thirty five degrees, double the degradation penalty for that cycle. Return the final health percentage rounded to one decimal place.

title: Tip Pool Distributor
spec: Write a `distribute(shift)` function that divides a total tip pool among restaurant staff based on their roles and hours worked. The input provides the total tips collected in dollars and a list of employee records containing their name, role, and hours worked. Bartenders receive a weight of two points per hour. Servers receive one and a half points per hour. Bussers receive one point per hour, and hosts receive zero point five points per hour. Calculate the total points for each employee by multiplying their hourly weight by their hours worked. Sum all points across the staff to find the total pool points. Divide the total tips by the total points to get the dollar value per point, then return a list of employee names and their calculated tip share rounded to the nearest cent.

title: Beer Bitterness Calculator
spec: Implement a `bitterness(recipe)` function that estimates the International Bitterness Units for a batch of beer. The input provides the batch volume in liters, the original gravity of the wort, and a list of hop additions. Each hop addition specifies the weight in grams, the alpha acid percentage, and the boil time in minutes. For each hop addition, calculate the utilization factor using a formula based on boil time and wort gravity. Multiply the hop weight by the alpha acid percentage, then by the utilization factor, and finally by ten, before dividing by the batch volume to get the units for that addition. Sum the units across all hop additions to get the total bitterness and return it rounded to the nearest whole number.

title: Knitting Pattern Scaler
spec: Write a `scale(pattern)` function that adjusts a knitting pattern for a different yarn gauge. The input specifies the original stitches per inch, the new stitches per inch, and a list of pattern instructions where each instruction contains an action like cast on or knit and a stitch count. For each instruction that involves a stitch count, calculate a multiplier by dividing the new gauge by the original gauge. Multiply the original stitch count by this multiplier and round to the nearest integer to get the new stitch count. Actions that do not have a stitch count should remain unchanged. Return the updated list of instructions with the newly calculated stitch counts.

title: Pipe Friction Loss
spec: Implement a `loss(system)` function to calculate the pressure drop due to friction in a water pipe network. The input is a list of pipe segments, each detailing the flow rate in liters per second, the pipe diameter in millimeters, the length in meters, and a friction factor. For each segment, calculate the fluid velocity by dividing the flow rate by the cross sectional area of the pipe. Then, compute the head loss using the Darcy Weisbach equation, which multiplies the friction factor by the pipe length divided by diameter, and then by the square of the velocity divided by twice the gravitational acceleration. Return the sum of head losses for all segments rounded to three decimal points.

title: Produce Quality Sorter
spec: Write a `grade(carrots)` function that categorizes a batch of harvested carrots. The input is a list of carrot records, each specifying length in centimeters, maximum diameter in millimeters, and a boolean indicating if there is a major visual defect. A carrot is graded as premium if it has no defects, length is between fifteen and twenty centimeters, and diameter is between twenty and thirty millimeters. It is graded as standard if it has no defects, length is at least ten centimeters, and diameter is at least fifteen millimeters. Any carrot with a major defect, or failing the standard size requirements, is graded as processing. Return a list containing the counts of premium, standard, and processing carrots.

title: Marathon Pace Strategy
spec: Implement a `pace(profile)` function that generates target split times for a marathon runner. The input provides a target finish time in minutes and a list of twenty six mile markers, each containing the elevation change in feet for that mile. First, determine the baseline flat pace by dividing the total time by twenty six point two. Then, adjust the pace for each mile based on the elevation change: add twelve seconds to the baseline pace for every one hundred feet of elevation gain, and subtract six seconds for every one hundred feet of elevation drop. Cap the maximum downhill pace benefit at twenty seconds per mile. Return a list of the target paces in minutes per mile for each of the twenty six miles.

title: Corporate Bond Yield
spec: Write a `yield(bond)` function to calculate the current yield and yield to maturity for a corporate bond. The input specifies the face value, the annual coupon rate as a percentage, the current market price, and the years remaining until maturity. First, determine the annual coupon payment by multiplying the face value by the coupon rate. Calculate the current yield by dividing the annual coupon payment by the current market price. Next, estimate the yield to maturity by adding the annual coupon payment to the difference between face value and market price divided by years to maturity, then dividing that sum by the average of the face value and market price. Return both calculated yields as percentages rounded to two decimal places.

title: Coastal Tide Estimator
spec: Implement an `estimate(tides)` function to approximate the water depth at a specific time between two tide extremes. The input provides the time and height of the previous tide extreme, the time and height of the next extreme, and the target time for the estimation, with all times in minutes since midnight. Calculate the total time duration between the two extremes and the elapsed time from the first extreme to the target time. Use the rule of twelfths to estimate the water level change: in the first sixth of the duration, the water level changes by one twelfth of the total range; in the second sixth, by two twelfths; and so on, peaking at three twelfths in the middle. Return the estimated water height at the target time.

title: Fertilizer Blend Formulator
spec: Write a `blend(requirements)` function that calculates the amount of raw materials needed to mix a custom agricultural fertilizer. The input defines the target mass in kilograms, and the target percentage of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. The available raw materials are urea for nitrogen, diammonium phosphate for phosphorus and some nitrogen, and muriate of potash for potassium. First, determine the total required mass of each nutrient. Calculate the required mass of diammonium phosphate to meet the phosphorus need, keeping in mind it also contributes nitrogen. Then, calculate the remaining nitrogen needed and fulfill it with urea. Finally, calculate the muriate of potash needed for potassium. Return a list containing the required masses of the three raw materials and any inert filler needed to reach the target mass.

title: Bicycle Spoke Calculator
spec: Implement a `length(wheel)` function that determines the exact required length for bicycle wheel spokes. The input specifies the effective rim diameter, the hub flange diameter, the distance from the hub center to the flange, the total number of spokes, and the number of crosses in the lacing pattern. First, calculate the spoke hole angle by dividing three hundred and sixty degrees by half the number of spokes, then multiplying by the cross pattern. Convert this angle to radians. Use the standard spoke length formula: take the square root of the sum of the square of half the rim diameter, the square of half the hub diameter, and the square of the hub center to flange distance, minus the product of the rim diameter, hub diameter, and the cosine of the spoke hole angle. Return the final length rounded to one decimal place.

title: Tea Steeping Optimizer
spec: Write an `optimize(parameters)` function that evaluates the quality of a tea brew based on time and temperature. The input is a list of brewing trials, where each trial provides the tea type, water temperature in Celsius, and steeping time in seconds. For green tea, the optimal temperature is between seventy and eighty degrees, and time is between one hundred and twenty and one hundred and eighty seconds. For black tea, temperature should be ninety to ninety five degrees, and time two hundred to three hundred seconds. For white tea, temperature is eighty to eighty five degrees, and time is up to one hundred and fifty seconds. For each trial, determine if it is under extracted, optimal, or over extracted based on these ranges. Return a list of the evaluations corresponding to each trial.

title: Room Cooling Load
spec: Implement a `load(room)` function that estimates the sensible cooling load for a room in British Thermal Units per hour. The input specifies the room floor area in square feet, the total window area, the number of occupants, and the amount of heat generated by electronics in watts. First, calculate the base structural load by multiplying the floor area by twenty. Then, calculate the solar gain by multiplying the window area by fifty. Add the occupant load, assuming each person contributes four hundred BTUs per hour. Finally, convert the electronics heat from watts to BTUs by multiplying by three point four one two. Sum these four components to find the total sensible cooling load and return it rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Concrete Mix Proportions
spec: Write a `mix(volume)` function that calculates the required weights of cement, sand, gravel, and water for a given volume of concrete. The input specifies the target volume in cubic meters and the desired compressive strength in megapascals. For a strength of twenty megapascals, the ratio of cement to sand to gravel by volume is one to two to four, with a water to cement weight ratio of zero point five. For thirty megapascals, the ratio is one to one point five to three, with a water ratio of zero point four five. Assume the density of cement is one thousand four hundred and forty kilograms per cubic meter, sand is one thousand six hundred, and gravel is one thousand five hundred. Return the weights of the four components in kilograms.

title: Ski Jump Scorer
spec: Implement a `score(jump)` function that calculates the final score for an individual ski jump. The input provides the jump distance in meters, the hill k-point in meters, the hill size category, and a list of five style marks given by judges out of twenty. First, determine the distance points: start with sixty points, then add or subtract points based on the difference between the jump distance and the k-point. For normal hills, the distance multiplier is two points per meter, and for large hills, it is one point eight points per meter. Next, calculate the style points by discarding the highest and lowest judges' marks and summing the remaining three. Add the distance points and style points together to get the final score, returning it as a decimal number.

title: Soil Moisture Deficit
spec: Write a `deficit(weather)` function that calculates the daily soil moisture deficit over a sequence of days. The input provides an initial moisture deficit in millimeters, the maximum soil capacity, and a list of daily records containing rainfall and evapotranspiration in millimeters. For each day, add the evapotranspiration to the current deficit, and subtract the rainfall. If the calculated deficit drops below zero, indicating the soil is fully saturated and water is lost to runoff, reset the deficit to zero. If the deficit exceeds the maximum soil capacity, cap it at that maximum value. Return a list of the daily ending deficit values. For an initial deficit of ten, cap of fifty, and two days with zero rain and five evapotranspiration, the output is fifteen, then twenty.

title: Mash Strike Water
spec: Implement a `temperature(mash)` function that calculates the necessary temperature of strike water to achieve a target mash temperature for brewing. The input specifies the target mash temperature in Celsius, the weight of the crushed grain in kilograms, the volume of strike water in liters, and the current temperature of the dry grain. First, calculate the thermal mass ratio by dividing the volume of water by the weight of the grain. Then, calculate the temperature differential by dividing the constant zero point four one by the thermal mass ratio, and multiplying the result by the difference between the target mash temperature and the dry grain temperature. Finally, add this differential to the target mash temperature to find the required strike water temperature. Return the final value rounded to one decimal place.

title: Astronomical Julian Date Calculator
spec: Implement the main function `calculate(date)` that receives a three element array containing the year, month, and day. First, adjust the year and month by subtracting one from the year and adding twelve to the month if the given month is January or February. Calculate the century leap year term by dividing the adjusted year by one hundred and manipulating the result. Calculate the yearly leap year term using the adjusted year and standard calendar constants. Add the day of the month to the accumulated total. Apply a fixed constant offset of one million seven hundred twenty thousand nine hundred ninety four point five. Check if the resulting date is before the Gregorian calendar adoption in fifteen eighty two, and apply a Julian calendar correction offset if necessary. Return the final Julian day number as a float. For example, an input of two thousand twenty three, ten, and four should return two million four hundred sixty thousand two hundred nineteen point five.

title: Wind Turbine Power Estimator
spec: Create the function `estimate(conditions)` that takes a three element array containing wind speed in meters per second, blade length in meters, and air density. Calculate the swept area of the turbine using pi and the square of the blade length. Check if the wind speed is below the cut in speed of three meters per second, returning zero if so. Check if the wind speed is above the cut out speed of twenty five meters per second, also returning zero to simulate automatic braking. Calculate the theoretical maximum power using half the air density, the swept area, and the cubed wind speed. Apply the Betz limit by multiplying by zero point fifty nine to account for maximum physical extraction. Apply a mechanical efficiency loss by subtracting ten percent from the remaining power. Check if the final power exceeds the generator maximum capacity of two thousand kilowatts, capping it at that limit if needed. Return the final generated power in kilowatts. For example, given ten, forty, and one point two, it yields a specific kilowatt numerical value.

title: Earthquake Magnitude Converter
spec: Write the function `convert(magnitude)` which accepts a single numeric value representing a Richter scale reading. Check if the magnitude is below zero, returning an array of four zeros immediately since negative readings are negligible. Calculate the seismic energy yield in joules using the standard logarithmic formula multiplying the magnitude by one point five and adding four point eight, then raising ten to that power. Convert the energy to tons of explosive equivalent by dividing the joule value by four point one eight four times ten to the power of nine. Determine the descriptive class string such as minor, moderate, strong, or major based on standard magnitude integer thresholds. Calculate the expected felt radius in kilometers using an exponential scaling factor based on the magnitude. Return an array containing the energy in joules, the explosive equivalent in tons, the descriptive class string, and the felt radius. An input of five point zero should return the calculated values and a string of moderate.

title: Audio File Bitrate Estimator
spec: Design the function `size(parameters)` that receives an array of four numbers representing duration in seconds, sample rate in hertz, bit depth, and channel count. Calculate the bits per sample by multiplying the bit depth and the channel count. Calculate the bits per second by multiplying the sample bits by the sample rate. Check if the bits per second exceeds a maximum streaming threshold of three hundred twenty thousand, capping it at that maximum to simulate automatic compression. Convert the total bits to bytes by dividing by eight. Multiply the bytes by the duration to find the total raw file size. Add a standard container header size of forty four bytes to the total. Convert the final byte size to megabytes by dividing by one million forty eight thousand five hundred seventy six. Return the megabyte value rounded to two decimal places. For example, given one hundred twenty, forty four thousand one hundred, sixteen, and two, it returns the total file size in megabytes.

title: Darts Score Calculator
spec: Develop the function `score(throws)` that accepts an array of arrays, where each inner array contains an integer point value and an integer multiplier. Start the game with a running score of five hundred and one. Iterate through each throw in the sequence. Multiply the raw points by the multiplier for the current throw to find the actual deduction. Check if the deduction strictly exceeds the current running score, in which case the throw is a bust and the turn ends without changing the score. Check if subtracting the deduction leaves exactly one point remaining, which is also an automatic bust. Check if the deduction reduces the score to exactly zero but the multiplier was not two, which again triggers a bust since games must end on a double. If the score becomes exactly zero and the multiplier was two, the game is won, so stop processing further throws immediately. Return the final remaining score after evaluating all throws. Given an input of arrays like twenty and three, followed by twenty and one, it deducts eighty points.

title: Blood Pressure Categorizer
spec: Write a function `categorize(readings)` that takes an array containing a systolic and a diastolic integer reading. Ensure both values are positive, returning a single element array with an invalid string if either is zero or negative. Check if the systolic is over one hundred eighty or the diastolic is over one hundred twenty, returning a crisis string. Check if the systolic is at least one hundred forty or the diastolic is at least ninety, returning a stage two string. Check if the systolic is at least one hundred thirty or the diastolic is at least eighty, returning a stage one string. Check if the systolic is at least one hundred twenty and the diastolic is strictly under eighty, returning an elevated string. If none of these conditions are met, meaning systolic is under one hundred twenty and diastolic is under eighty, assign a normal string. Calculate the pulse pressure by subtracting the diastolic from the systolic. Return an array containing the assigned string category and the calculated pulse pressure.

title: Diamond Valuation Estimator
spec: Create the function `appraise(attributes)` which receives an array containing carat weight, color index, clarity index, and cut index. Calculate the base dollar value by squaring the carat weight and multiplying by a standard base price of four thousand. Determine the color discount by multiplying the color index by a fixed depreciation percentage and subtracting that amount from the base value. Calculate the clarity premium by applying a quadratic multiplier to the clarity index and adding it to the running total. Check if the cut index is below a minimum acceptable threshold of three, applying a severe flat penalty of five hundred dollars if true. Add a collector premium of ten percent if the carat weight is perfectly round like exactly one point zero or two point zero. Ensure the final appraised value does not fall below a scrap minimum of two hundred dollars. Return the final estimated dollar value.

title: Baking Sourdough Schedule
spec: Implement `timetable(conditions)` which takes an array of three numbers representing the start hour in twenty four hour format, ambient room temperature in Celsius, and starter hydration percentage. Determine the autolyse phase duration, which is fixed at one hour regardless of conditions. Calculate the bulk fermentation time, starting with a base of six hours and subtracting half an hour for every degree the room temperature is above twenty Celsius. Adjust the bulk time based on the starter percentage, decreasing it by an additional hour if the hydration is above eighty percent. Determine the shaping and bench rest phase, adding a flat one hour to the timeline. Calculate the cold retard duration, setting it to twelve hours as a standard overnight refrigeration. Sum all individual phase durations to find the total process time. Add the total process time to the start hour and apply modulo twenty four to find the final baking hour. Return an array containing the calculated bulk time, total process time, and the final baking hour.

title: Lumber Board Foot Calculator
spec: Design the function `estimate(boards)` that accepts an array of arrays, where each sub array contains thickness in inches, width in inches, length in feet, and wood species density in pounds per cubic foot. Initialize a total board feet counter and a total weight counter to zero. Loop over each board in the given list. Calculate the individual board feet by multiplying thickness, width, and length, then dividing by twelve. Add the individual board feet to the total counter. Calculate the physical volume in cubic feet and multiply by the species density to find the board weight. Add the board weight to the total weight counter. Check if the total board feet exceeds one thousand, which qualifies the order for a ten percent bulk wholesale discount on the final cost. Calculate the final material cost based on a base rate of five dollars per board foot, applying the discount if earned. Return a three element array containing total board feet, total weight, and final cost.

title: Typing Speed Evaluator
spec: Develop the function `evaluate(session)` that takes a three element array containing total keystrokes, incorrect keystrokes, and elapsed time in minutes. Calculate the gross words typed by dividing the total keystrokes by a standard word length of five. Calculate the gross words per minute by dividing the gross words by the elapsed time. Calculate the net words typed by subtracting the incorrect keystrokes from the total keystrokes and then dividing by five. Calculate the net words per minute by dividing the net words by the elapsed time. Check if the net words per minute evaluates to a negative number, resetting it to zero to prevent negative scores on terrible runs. Calculate the accuracy percentage by dividing correct keystrokes by total keystrokes and multiplying by one hundred. Determine a performance tier string such as slow, average, or fast based on thresholds applied to the net words per minute. Return an array containing the net words per minute, the accuracy percentage, and the tier string.

title: Sailing Handicap Scorer
spec: Write `score(boats)` which receives an array of arrays, each holding a boat identification number, elapsed race seconds, and a specific boat class rating factor. Create an empty result list to hold processed entries. Iterate through each boat in the provided roster. Calculate the corrected finish time by multiplying the elapsed seconds by the rating factor. Check if the elapsed seconds value is exactly zero, marking the boat as a non finisher and setting its corrected time to an artificially massive penalty number. Push the identification number and the corrected time into the result list. Sort the result list based on the corrected time in ascending order so the lowest time is first. Extract just the sorted identification numbers into a new placements list. Calculate the time difference in seconds between the first place and second place corrected times. Return an array containing the sorted placements list and the time gap to second place.

title: HVAC Ductwork Sizing
spec: Implement `size(network)` taking an array of three numbers for total airflow volume in cubic feet per minute, duct length in feet, and maximum allowed air velocity in feet per minute. Calculate the required duct cross sectional area in square feet by dividing the total airflow volume by the maximum allowed air velocity. Convert the required cross sectional area to square inches by multiplying by one hundred forty four. Calculate the theoretical circular duct diameter from the area using the standard circle formula. Round the theoretical diameter up to the nearest standard commercial duct size from a predetermined list of even numbers like eight, ten, twelve, or fourteen inches. Calculate the friction pressure loss per hundred feet based on the chosen standard diameter and the calculated airflow. Multiply the pressure loss by the actual duct length divided by one hundred to get the total static pressure drop. Check if the total pressure drop exceeds the available fan pressure of two inches of water gauge, returning an error flag if so. Return an array of the chosen standard diameter and the total pressure drop.

title: Carrot Harvesting Yield
spec: Create the function `yield(field)` that receives an array containing field size in acres, row spacing in inches, plant spacing in inches, and average root weight in grams. Convert the field area from acres to square feet by multiplying by forty three thousand five hundred sixty. Calculate the number of linear crop rows by dividing the square root of the area by the row spacing converted to feet. Calculate plants per row by dividing the row length by the plant spacing converted to feet. Multiply the number of rows by the plants per row to determine the total plant population. Multiply the total population by the average root weight to compute the total harvest weight in grams. Convert the total weight from grams to metric tons by dividing by one million. Subtract a flat five percent loss factor to account for mechanical field damage during harvesting. Return the final estimated metric tons rounded to one decimal place.

title: Drone Flight Range Estimator
spec: Design `range(specs)` which takes an array of five numbers representing battery capacity in milliamp hours, system voltage, cruise draw in amps, standard speed in meters per second, and headwind in meters per second. Convert battery capacity to total watt hours by multiplying milliamp hours by voltage and dividing by one thousand. Calculate total cruise power consumption by multiplying the cruise draw amps by the system voltage. Calculate maximum theoretical flight time in hours by dividing watt hours by cruise power. Convert the flight time into seconds for distance calculations. Adjust the drone ground speed by subtracting the headwind speed from the standard speed. Check if the adjusted ground speed is zero or negative, which means the drone cannot make forward progress, and immediately return zero range. Multiply the adjusted ground speed by the flight time in seconds to get the total range in meters. Convert the range to kilometers and subtract a ten percent safety reserve to ensure a safe landing. Return the final safe range in kilometers.

title: Hair Dye Mixing Ratio
spec: Write `formulate(client)` taking an array of natural hair level, target hair level, grey percentage, and hair length in inches. Calculate the required levels of lift by subtracting the natural level from the target level. Determine the developer volume needed, starting at a ten volume baseline and adding ten for each level of required lift. Cap the developer strength strictly at forty volume to prevent severe chemical damage to the hair. Calculate the base color mass starting at a baseline of thirty grams, adding ten additional grams for every full five inches of hair length. Adjust the base color mass if the grey percentage is above fifty, increasing the mass by twenty percent for dense, opaque coverage. Calculate the required developer mass using a standard one to one point five chemical mixing ratio against the final base color mass. Round both calculated masses to the nearest whole gram. Return an array containing the developer volume, the color mass in grams, and the developer mass in grams.

title: Amusement Park Queue Simulator
spec: Develop `simulate(ride)` taking an array of four numbers representing current people in line, ride capacity per dispatch, dispatch interval in minutes, and fast pass allocation ratio. Calculate the effective standard capacity by subtracting the expected fast pass riders from the total capacity per dispatch using the allocation ratio. Check if the effective capacity drops to zero or below, meaning standard guests never board, and return a negative error code. Divide the current people in line by the effective standard capacity to find the total number of dispatch cycles required. Multiply the required cycles by the dispatch interval to calculate the raw wait time in minutes. Add a ten percent time buffer to account for slow loading guests and minor operational delays. Check if the final wait time exceeds a maximum display value of one hundred twenty minutes, capping it at that limit for the public park app. Round the final wait time up to the nearest multiple of five minutes for cleaner display. Return the posted wait time.

title: Radio Frequency Link Budget
spec: Implement `budget(link)` receiving an array containing transmit power in decibels, frequency in megahertz, distance in kilometers, transmitter antenna gain, and receiver antenna gain. Calculate the free space path loss using the standard radio formula multiplying twenty times the base ten logarithm of the distance and frequency, plus a constant offset of thirty two point four four. Add the transmit power to the transmitter antenna gain to determine the effective isotropic radiated power. Subtract the calculated free space path loss from the radiated power to simulate signal attenuation over the atmospheric distance. Add the receiver antenna gain to the attenuated signal to find the final received signal strength at the destination. Check if the received power falls below the receiver hardware sensitivity threshold of negative ninety decibels, setting a boolean failure flag to true if it does. Calculate the fade margin by subtracting the sensitivity threshold from the received power. Return an array with the received power, the fade margin, and the failure flag.

title: Cardio Training Zones
spec: Create `zones(athlete)` that takes an array containing age and resting heart rate. Calculate the estimated maximum heart rate by subtracting the age from the standard physiological constant of two hundred and twenty. Calculate the heart rate reserve by subtracting the resting heart rate from the maximum heart rate. Determine the zone one threshold by multiplying the reserve by fifty percent and adding back the resting rate. Determine the zone two threshold by multiplying the reserve by sixty percent and adding back the resting rate. Determine the zone three threshold by multiplying the reserve by seventy percent and adding back the resting rate. Determine the zone four threshold by multiplying the reserve by eighty percent and adding back the resting rate. Determine the zone five threshold by multiplying the reserve by ninety percent and adding back the resting rate. Round all five calculated zone thresholds to the nearest whole beat per minute. Return an array containing the five integer thresholds in ascending order.

title: Textile Loom Production
spec: Design `production(loom)` receiving an array with picks per inch, loom speed in picks per minute, run time in hours, efficiency percentage, and number of color changes. Multiply the loom speed by sixty to determine theoretical picks per hour. Multiply the hourly picks by the run time to find the absolute total theoretical picks. Multiply the theoretical picks by the efficiency percentage to account for minor mechanical stops and thread breakages. Calculate downtime for color changes by multiplying the number of color changes by a standard fifteen minute setup delay. Subtract the total color change downtime from the effective run time to find active weaving hours. Recalculate the actual produced picks based on the reduced active weaving hours and the loom speed. Divide the actual picks by the picks per inch to calculate the total inches of fabric woven. Divide the total inches by thirty six to convert the measurement to total yards of fabric. Return the total yards rounded down to the nearest whole number.

title: Gold Purity Assayer
spec: Write `assay(sample)` taking an array of sample weight in grams, karat rating, and current gold market price per gram. Calculate the purity percentage by dividing the karat rating by the maximum possible value of twenty four. Multiply the total sample weight by the purity percentage to find the exact weight of pure gold contained in the alloy. Deduct a two percent margin of error from the pure weight to account for impurities and chemical testing inaccuracies.
